To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the affordance system and mirror system are two different systems that share a common architecture and function, and that both are based on the exploitation of a hierarchical organisation of action and action-goals.

(a) mirror systems and affordance systems are two distinct but interacting systems; (b) mirror systems are hierarchically organized and are involved in the selection of actions; (c) affordance systems are hierarchially organized and are involved with the selection of action-goals; and (d) mirror systems and the affordance systems interact to support the selection of actions and action-goais.
the mirror system and affordance systems are two complementary systems that work together in a hierarchical manner to solve the two challenges mentioned above.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computational theory of affordance and mirroring that can be used to guide the development of new models and experimental paradigms in the domain of social cognition.
the study of the mechanisms that allow organisms to select among multiple actions and action-goal representations, and to use them to achieve complex goals.
the design of a framework for the analysis and modelling of the mechanisms and processes underlying affordance and mirror system functioning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two challenges we have described are solved by two distinct but related systems: the mirror system, which is specialised in selecting among affordances and possible goals, and the affordance system, specialised in exploiting the advantages deriving from hierarchical organisation of behaviour.
mirror systems are a part of a more general system that allows organisms to deal with the two challenges described above.
the affordance-mirror system is a complex and dynamic system, which is still far from being fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the affordance and mirror system theories can be integrated into one single theory, which is based on a hierarchical organisation of the brain and behaviour.
the two systems are tightly linked and that the mirror system is a part of the affordance system.
the affordances of an object are not fixed but depend on the organism's current goals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the affordances of an object are the set of actions the object affords, which in turn depend on the organism’s current goals and its current state.
the affordance and mirror system literature is best interpreted and modelled by considering the challenges that the systems solve and their interplay.
the two systems are tightly interwoven in the brain and that their interaction can be understood as a mechanism for hierarchical control of behaviour.
